explained.tdh.glossary.meta.title: Glossary: every TDH term · 6529 Explained
explained.tdh.glossary.meta.description: Every term the TDH chapter uses, with one meaning, its status and its source.
explained.tdh.glossary.title: Glossary
explained.tdh.glossary.lede: Every term the TDH chapter uses, with one meaning, its status and its source.
explained.tdh.glossary.table: TDH terms, their meanings, status and sources
explained.tdh.glossary.tdh.def: Total Days Held: for every eligible copy, whole days held × its card's rate, times one boost, recomputed daily.
explained.tdh.glossary.v14.def: The name of the rules 6529.io runs, since {since}; rule version {version} in the specification, which took the same name on {renamed}. The earlier schedules are under {versions}.
explained.tdh.glossary.p26.def: The TDH v1.4 specification: an exact restatement of the rules, with conformance vectors.
explained.tdh.glossary.memes.def: The three collections TDH counts: The Memes, cards of many copies each; 6529 Gradients, one copy each; and NextGen, whose tokens are weighed by the size of their own collection.
explained.tdh.glossary.cc0.def: A public-domain dedication. The Memes are dedicated under CC0, so anyone may copy, remix and sell the art without asking and without crediting the artist; owning a card gives no exclusive right to its image. It releases only the artist's own rights.
explained.tdh.glossary.card.def: A card is one artwork; a copy is one token of it. Wallets hold copies.
explained.tdh.glossary.edition.def: A card's copy count. For TDH, the effective edition: the copies minted, and below {threshold} the claim limit, at most {cap}. Never the collection 6529 Stream Editions, which is always named in full.
explained.tdh.glossary.firstgm.def: Meme #{id}, the reference card: {minted} minted, counted as {edition} after a recorded burn. While its edition is the largest, it sets every rate, and its own is {rate}.
explained.tdh.glossary.threshold.def: The smallest edition a release of The Memes ends with, {threshold} copies: below it, a final airdrop tops the card up. One of The Memes' two absolutes, with CC0. The rate formula does not assume it: a card with no claim gets no floor.
explained.tdh.glossary.claimLimit.def: The most copies a card's mint, a Manifold claim, allows, read from Ethereum at the cutoff block. While fewer than the threshold are minted, a card counts as if it had its claim limit, at most {cap}; a card with no claim has none.
explained.tdh.glossary.rate.def: {h} divided by a card's effective edition, computed in whole cents and shown in TDH: {rate} for {cap} copies.
explained.tdh.glossary.raw.def: Whole days summed over every copy held, before any weighting. The rate turns raw days into base TDH.
explained.tdh.glossary.base.def: A card's whole days times its rate, rounded to a whole number, before the boost.
explained.tdh.glossary.boost.def: One multiplier on everything an identity holds, from complete seasons, sets, Genesis, Nakamoto and Gradients. Never a drop's flame boost.
explained.tdh.glossary.season.def: A run of consecutive Meme ids, from a start the registry lists. A complete season adds {bonus} to the boost once the next one has begun, for seasons up to {last}.
explained.tdh.glossary.fullSet.def: At least one copy of every eligible Meme. It pays the bonus of every boostable season at once; each further set adds a smaller extra bonus.
explained.tdh.glossary.final.def: A card's base TDH times the boost, rounded to a whole number. An identity's TDH is the sum of its cards' finals.
explained.tdh.glossary.cycle.def: One day's computation. Cycle N is day N counted from the Unix epoch: its snapshot is the last block before midnight UTC on that day, and the result is dated by it and counts the day before. Cycle {cycle} is dated {date}.
explained.tdh.glossary.snapshot.def: The last Ethereum block before a cycle's midnight. Holdings are read as of this block, and ages are measured to its time.
explained.tdh.glossary.finalized.def: An Ethereum block that can no longer be reverted. A day has a result only once the block after its snapshot block is finalized.
explained.tdh.glossary.identity.def: Up to {max} wallets counted as one collector; past {ungated}, only with fresh two-way links from {gate}. A profile is the page; an identity is what is counted.
explained.tdh.glossary.consolidation.def: Wallets that register each other both ways on the delegation contract, so they count as one identity.
explained.tdh.glossary.pairkey.def: A link's name: its two wallets' addresses in lowercase, sorted and joined with a hyphen. When a group could form more than one way, links are taken newest block first, and links confirmed in one block in the order of their pair keys.
explained.tdh.glossary.delegation.def: A one-way grant to another wallet. It does not consolidate.
explained.tdh.glossary.xtdh.def: A separate score on 6529.io: what other holders grant you, plus what the cards you hold produce and you have not granted away. Never TDH, never validator weight.
explained.tdh.glossary.burn.def: The zero address and {dead}. Copies sent there are burned; they keep records but are never debited or consolidated. Their TDH counts in the feed's total; validators will sign the total without them.
explained.tdh.glossary.netting.def: Within one transaction, each address's movements of a token are added up, and only the net change moves holdings: a copy that leaves and comes back in one transaction never left.
explained.tdh.glossary.stack.def: For one card in one wallet, the times its copies were acquired, in order. A send removes the copies received last, and each copy's whole days come from its time.
explained.tdh.glossary.underflow.def: The check that no wallet ever sends a copy it does not hold. An input that fails it has no result.
explained.tdh.glossary.registry.def: Every number and address the rules use, fixed for each rule version and named by its hash.
explained.tdh.glossary.vector.def: A small input with its exact expected outputs. P26 has {count}; a program conforms when it reproduces every one.
explained.tdh.glossary.lean.def: A model of P26's rules written in Lean, a proof assistant; that it says what P26 says is tested by the vectors, not proved. A theorem is a statement about the model whose proof Lean's kernel checks at every build; the manifest has {count}, {tdh} about TDH and the rest about separate models of the validator rules (P53).
explained.tdh.glossary.axioms.def: Lean's kernel is the small checker every proof passes through. Each theorem may rest only on Lean's three standard axioms. That the kernel and the axioms are sound is assumed, not proved.
explained.tdh.glossary.counterexample.de: A claim refuted on one concrete input, and kept on the page beside the claim it refutes. Shown false in Lean's kernel, or by evaluating the model, which trusts Lean's compiler.
explained.tdh.glossary.limit.def: What a proof does not cover, named in the manifest beside the claims it bounds.
explained.tdh.glossary.zk.def: A short proof that a program ran on its input and gave its output, checked without running it again. Nothing about the day is hidden: what is used is that the proof is small and cheap to check. Proof A is program A in SP1, proof B is program B in RISC Zero; the contract would accept a day only with both.
explained.tdh.glossary.zkvm.def: A zero-knowledge virtual machine: it runs an ordinary program and makes a proof that it ran. SP1 runs program A; RISC Zero, from other makers on other libraries, runs program B.
explained.tdh.glossary.groth16.def: The last step of each proof: a few hundred bytes that Ethereum can check cheaply, on the BN254 curve Ethereum supports. As built today both proofs use it, so a break of the curve would reach both. P52, a proposal not adopted, recommends another wrapper for program B; that is open.
explained.tdh.glossary.tproof.term: T proof, proof A, proof B
explained.tdh.glossary.tproof.def: The design record's name for a zero-knowledge proof of one day's TDH, whose public statement is {words} words. These pages call the two proofs of a day proof A and proof B, after the programs that make them.
explained.tdh.glossary.halfPair.def: The mark for a day proved by one of its two programs: proof A done, proof B not yet. The contract would record a day only with both.
explained.tdh.glossary.word.def: One {bytes}-byte value of a proof's public statement, in Ethereum's ABI encoding. The statement is {words} words: the day, the rule, where the day starts and ends, the anchor, what it read and the result.
explained.tdh.glossary.anchor.def: A later block whose hash Ethereum itself reports. Every header from the day's start is hashed forward to it, so the blocks are Ethereum's and not made up. Checking it against Ethereum is the contract's step; a read-only call to a verifier does not.
explained.tdh.glossary.bloom.def: A short summary in each block's header of the contracts and topics its logs touch. It never misses one that is there, so a bloom that rules a contract out proves the block has no log of it. When it cannot rule them out, every receipt is rebuilt instead.
explained.tdh.glossary.readonly.def: Asking a contract on mainnet a question without sending a transaction: nothing is recorded and nothing is paid. It shows that mainnet's verifier accepts a proof; it records no day.
explained.tdh.glossary.horizon.def: The last moment a build of the proof programs covers, {horizon}: past it Ethereum may change its rules, so each program must be built again and a new contract deployed to record later days.
explained.tdh.glossary.root.def: A hash that commits to a day's result: the day, its snapshot block, the rule version and every record. Equal records give equal roots; it is the root validators sign.
explained.tdh.glossary.comparison.def: Every day the Rust core and the Python reference recompute every identity's TDH and compare it with 6529.io. Both read one input file, written by the Rust core, so they do not check what was read. Its files are hashed, not signed; 6529.io's own upload is signed.
explained.tdh.glossary.classes.def: How the daily comparison sorts a difference: A, a deliberate difference from 6529.io's old code; B, a bug in that code; C, the two recomputations disagree; D, no known cause, which raises an alarm.
explained.tdh.glossary.knowncause.def: A day's verdict when records differ and each difference has a known cause, class A or B. Formerly “Explained”.
explained.tdh.glossary.simulated.def: The tag on a state built to show what a failure would look like, such as a day that fails or a pair the contract refuses. Its numbers are constructed, never read from a file.
explained.tdh.glossary.cutover.def: The day 6529.io switches from its current backend to the Rust core's result, about {about}.
explained.tdh.glossary.cutover.defLate: The day 6529.io switches from its current backend to the Rust core's result. Planned for about {about}; as of {checked}, not made.
explained.tdh.glossary.programs.def: Two separately written TDH programs; A is the Rust core. Proof A and proof B are each program run inside a zero-knowledge prover. The Python and Rust references were written from P26 as well.
explained.tdh.glossary.validator.def: Software that reads Ethereum, computes the day and signs one root. Version {version}: built, being tested; so far only 6529's own validators sign, in testing.
explained.tdh.glossary.items.def: {d} is one of the owner's decisions; {dev} one of the specification's deviations from 6529.io's old code; {bug} one of that code's issues.
explained.tdh.glossary.nic.def: Network Identity Check: a rating collectors give each other's profiles, with its own budget. A rating, never a credit.
explained.tdh.glossary.hwk.definitionsBo: 6529.io's code and copy, the specification, and 6529's design glossary.
explained.tdh.glossary.hwk.wordsBody: Edition, boost, identity and Explained, each held to one meaning here.
